about: Escrito a mano (no lo genera build.py): resúmenes modelo de las lecturas graduadas, lectura recomendada y texto del dictogloss de cada unidad del curso.

summaries.a1-hello-lucia: Lucía is a student from Argentina. She lives in London with two friends. She likes music and coffee, but she doesn't like rainy days.
summaries.a1-my-day: Ben is a nurse in Manchester. He gets up at six and goes to work by bus. In the evening he cooks dinner and watches TV with his wife.
summaries.a1-family-photo: It is a photo of a family at the grandmother's 80th birthday. We see the grandparents, the parents, the brother and the dog. The writer is not in the photo because the writer has the camera.
summaries.a1-cafe: The Blue Café is a small café in Bristol. It has breakfast, soup, sandwiches and cakes. It is cheap and friendly, and students study there because it has free wifi.
summaries.a1-my-town: Hayfield is a small, quiet town in the north of England. It has a supermarket, schools and a station, but no cinema. The writer likes the friendly people and the walks, but there isn't much to do at night.
summaries.a1-park-sunday: It is a sunny Sunday in Green Park. People are feeding ducks, running, having a picnic and singing. The writer is sitting on the grass and writing.
summaries.a2-edinburgh: The writer spent a weekend in Edinburgh with a sister. They went by train, visited the castle, walked down the Royal Mile and tried haggis. On Sunday they went to a museum and climbed Arthur's Seat, the best part of the trip. They want to go back.
summaries.a2-healthy-week: The writer's doctor gave some advice about health, so the writer tried a healthy week: walking to work, sleeping more, cooking at home and doing yoga. The weekend was difficult, but now the writer has more energy and feels happier.
summaries.a2-host-family: The writer lived with a family in Dublin for two months while studying English. There were a few rules, and at first it was hard to understand them. The family dinners were the best part, and living with them helped a lot with English.
summaries.a2-lost-phone: The writer fell asleep on a train and lost a phone. The writer called the number from a laptop, and later a woman called Grace answered. They met the next day, and the writer bought her a coffee and cake to say thank you.
summaries.a2-new-neighbour: The writer was worried about a new neighbour, an old woman who lived alone. The writer helped her move her piano and learned she was a music teacher who travelled the world. Now they are good friends and help each other.
summaries.a2-summer-plans: Sam writes to Maya about the summer. Sam is going to work in an uncle's restaurant, travel around Portugal with a cousin and take a guitar course. Sam invites Maya to visit at the end of August.
summaries.b1-digital-nomads: Marta left her bank job in Madrid and now works as a web designer while she travels. Remote work has become common since 2020, and some countries offer special visas. But the lifestyle has problems: long hours, loneliness, taxes and higher rents for local people.
summaries.b1-car-free-village: Giethoorn is a Dutch village with almost no roads: people use boats, bikes and bridges. The canals were dug long ago to transport peat. Visitors love the peace, but life without cars is not easy and tourism can be too much. Planners see it as an inspiration for car-free streets.
summaries.b1-learning-to-cook: The writer couldn't cook until moving to Wales and living alone. The writer's grandmother taught them on the phone, starting with lentil soup. They had a cooking call every Sunday, and the writer learned that cooking is about patience and sharing. Her advice is still in the writer's notebook.
summaries.b1-social-media-lonely: Many people feel lonely even though we are very connected. Research suggests that passive scrolling makes people feel worse, while active use and real meetings help. Experts recommend simple habits, because technology is neither good nor bad: it depends on how we use it.
summaries.b1-bonfire-night: Bonfire Night on 5 November remembers the failed Gunpowder Plot of 1605 against King James I. People lit bonfires to celebrate, and the tradition continues with fireworks and food. However, fireworks can frighten animals and cause injuries, so many people prefer organised events.
summaries.b1-volunteer-diary: The writer spent a month volunteering at a turtle conservation centre in Costa Rica. The volunteers patrolled the beach at night, protected turtle eggs and cleaned plastic from the beach. Seeing the baby turtles reach the sea taught the writer that small actions can make a difference.
summaries.b2-four-day-week: A large UK trial in 2022 tested a four-day week with no loss of pay, and most companies decided to keep it. Workers were less stressed and took fewer sick days. Critics say the companies were mostly small offices and that the model is harder for hospitals or factories. The debate makes us ask whether we should measure results rather than hours.
summaries.b2-fake-news: An MIT study found that false news spreads faster and further than true news, mainly because of human users. False stories are surprising and emotional, and confirmation bias and repetition make us believe them. Simple habits, such as checking the source before sharing, reduce the problem, which is human as much as technological.
summaries.b2-night-trains: Night trains almost disappeared because of cheap flights, but they have come back since Austria's Nightjet took over German routes. Climate awareness is the main reason, but travellers also enjoy the experience and save on hotels. High costs, sold-out services and delays are still problems, so their future depends on investment.
summaries.b2-rewilding: Rewilding tries to restore natural processes instead of only protecting what is left. Returning species such as beavers improves whole ecosystems, while wolves are more controversial because of farmers. Rewilding can create jobs, but critics worry about lost farmland. The best projects work with local communities.
summaries.b2-habits: Resolutions often fail because people misunderstand how habits work: a cue, a routine and a reward. A study found that a new habit takes about sixty-six days on average, with big differences between people. Good strategies are starting small, linking habits, making them easy and rewarding them, and thinking about identity.
summaries.b2-last-letter: Eleanor receives a handwritten letter with an old photo of herself. It is from Daniel, who didn't come to the station fifty years ago because he was afraid. She had left for Canada and had a happy life there. After thinking about it, she starts writing a kind reply and invites him for tea.

dictogloss.en-a1-u01: Hello! My name is Sam. I'm twenty years old and I'm a student. This is my friend Mia. She's nineteen. How are you today? We're fine, thank you. Nice to meet you!
dictogloss.en-a1-u02: Paolo is from Italy. He's a chef in a restaurant in London. His friends Yuki and Ken are from Japan. They're nurses. Are you a nurse? No, I'm not. I'm a teacher, and I'm from Spain.
dictogloss.en-a1-u03: This is my family. My father is tall and he's got short brown hair. My mother has got long hair and blue eyes. I've got a sister, but I haven't got a brother. My sister's name is Emma.
dictogloss.en-a1-u04: Tom gets up at seven o'clock every day. He has breakfast at half past seven and he takes the bus to work. He doesn't work on Saturdays. Does he go to the gym? Yes, he goes on Mondays and Fridays.
dictogloss.en-a1-u05: I like fruit and vegetables, but I don't like fish. For breakfast I have some bread and an apple. Is there any milk? No, there isn't any. Can I have a coffee and two sandwiches, please?
dictogloss.en-a1-u06: My flat is small but nice. There is a living room, a kitchen and one bedroom. There are two chairs in the kitchen. My bed is next to the window, and my books are on a white shelf.
dictogloss.en-a1-u07: Excuse me, where is the station? Go straight on and turn left at the bank. The station is opposite the museum. It's about ten minutes on foot, or you can take the number five bus.
dictogloss.en-a1-u08: These shoes are thirty-five pounds and that blue jacket is ninety. How much is this T-shirt? It's twelve pounds fifty. I'd like those black trousers too, please. Can I pay by card?
dictogloss.en-a1-u09: I can swim and I can play the guitar, but I can't dance! Right now my brother is playing football in the park and my parents are watching TV. Would you like to come to the cinema tonight?
dictogloss.en-a1-u10: It's cold and windy today, and it's raining. My birthday is on the fifteenth of March. This weekend I'm visiting my grandparents in the country. In August we're going to the beach.
dictogloss.en-a1-u11: Where's my phone? It isn't on the table. Is it in your bag? There's a pen and an umbrella in the bag, but there isn't a phone. Oh, here it is, under the sofa! Please close the door.
dictogloss.en-a2-u01: Last Saturday I got up late and had a big breakfast. In the afternoon I went to the market with my friend Lucy and we bought some fruit. I didn't go out in the evening. I watched a film and went to bed early.
dictogloss.en-a2-u02: Last summer we went to Greece for two weeks. We flew from Madrid and stayed in a small hotel near the sea. Every morning we swam in the sea, and at night we ate fresh fish. Did you go on holiday this year?
dictogloss.en-a2-u03: My new town is bigger than my old one, but it isn't as friendly. The streets are busier and the houses are more expensive. The best thing is the park. It's the biggest park in the region and it's never too crowded.
dictogloss.en-a2-u04: We haven't got much rice, but there are a lot of potatoes. How many eggs do we need for the cake? Three, and a little sugar. There isn't any butter, so can you buy some at the supermarket on your way home?
dictogloss.en-a2-u05: Next year I'm going to study in Canada. I'm going to live with a family, so I think my English will improve quickly. It might be cold in winter, but I'm sure I'll love it. Will you visit me?
dictogloss.en-a2-u06: I've got a bad cold and a sore throat. The doctor says I should stay in bed and drink a lot of water. I have to take this medicine three times a day, and I mustn't go to work until Friday.
dictogloss.en-a2-u07: I work at a hotel reception. I usually start at eight, but this week I'm working nights because a colleague is on holiday. I answer the phone, check guests in and send a lot of emails. I really enjoy meeting people.
dictogloss.en-a2-u08: Have you ever been to Japan? I've been there twice. I went for the first time in 2019. I've already visited Tokyo and Kyoto, but I haven't seen Mount Fuji yet. I've wanted to climb it for years.
dictogloss.en-a2-u09: I was walking home when my phone rang. While I was talking to my sister, I dropped it in a puddle! Now it doesn't work. Is this charger yours or mine? I need to send a message to my boss.
dictogloss.en-a2-u10: I think learning languages is great fun. I enjoy listening to music in English, and I want to travel more. I was nervous at first, but now I speak more confidently because I practise every day. I'm proud of my progress.
dictogloss.en-a2-u11: Excuse me, can I try on this jacket? It's too small. Have you got it in a large? I bought these jeans last week, but they've got a hole. I'd like to return them, please. Here's my receipt.
dictogloss.en-a2-u12: The train to Oxford leaves from platform four, but it's twenty minutes late. You can also take the coach. Get off at the third stop, cross the road and walk past the church. The museum is on your right.
dictogloss.en-a2-u13: I play tennis twice a week and I go swimming on Sundays. Last month I joined a photography club. The meetings are interesting, and I'm never bored. We usually take photos in the city centre and share them online.
dictogloss.en-b1-u01: My grandfather has been working in his garden since he retired, and he has grown everything from tomatoes to roses. When he was young, he used to work on fishing boats and he would leave home before sunrise. By the time he was thirty, he had sailed around the world twice.
dictogloss.en-b1-u02: I live in a neighbourhood which used to be quite dangerous, but it has changed a lot. The woman who runs the café on the corner organises a street party every summer. The more people get involved, the friendlier the area becomes. It's the place where I feel most at home.
dictogloss.en-b1-u03: When I finish my degree, I'd like to work in marketing. Last year I did an internship at a small company, where I had to write reports and manage social media. It was hard at first, but I managed to finish an important project on time, and they offered me a job.
dictogloss.en-b1-u04: If you sleep well, you'll have more energy during the day. Doctors say you shouldn't look at screens before bed, and you'd better avoid coffee in the evening. You can eat a little chocolate, as long as you don't eat too much. Unless you exercise regularly, you won't feel the difference.
dictogloss.en-b1-u05: Most smartphones are designed in one country and made in another. The first text message was sent in 1992. Today, millions of posts are shared every minute, and many news stories are read online before they appear in newspapers. But who decides which ones we see?
dictogloss.en-b1-u06: If I won the lottery, I would travel around South America for a year. I wish I could speak Spanish better, because I'd love to talk to local people. The last time I went abroad, the hotel lost my booking and I had to sleep at the airport. Now I always check everything twice.
dictogloss.en-b1-u07: My neighbour told me that she had bought a new laptop online. She said it had arrived broken, so she called customer service. They asked her if she had kept the box and suggested sending it back. A week later, she told me that they had refunded all her money.
dictogloss.en-b1-u08: At my school we weren't allowed to use phones in class, and we were supposed to do two hours of homework every day. I stopped studying with music because I couldn't concentrate. Now I stop to take a short break every hour, and I remember much more.
dictogloss.en-b1-u09: Most people agree that plastic is a problem, but not all of them change their habits. Both my parents recycle, and neither of them buys bottled water. The weather has been so strange this year that it might snow in April. We all need to do something, however small.
dictogloss.en-b1-u10: In my town, the spring festival must be more than three hundred years old. Nobody stays at home, and anyone can join the parade. Everyone eats sweet bread and dances in the square. Someone always plays the drums until midnight. It's a wonderful tradition, isn't it?
dictogloss.en-b1-u11: My best friend and I fell out last month because I forgot her birthday. I should have called her, but I was too busy. I see why she was upset. Last week we met for coffee and made up. We've always got on well, and I don't want to lose her.
dictogloss.en-b1-u12: Although she was born with a hearing problem, Ana became a professional musician. Despite the difficulties, she never stopped practising. When people told her it was impossible, she simply worked harder. She has now played in more than twenty countries, and she teaches children with similar challenges.
dictogloss.en-b2-u01: This time next year, I'll be living in a city I've never visited. My sister, who moved to Rome five years ago, says the hardest part isn't the language but the small habits. She's got used to dinner at nine, but she still isn't used to the traffic. I'm curious to see how much I'll change.
dictogloss.en-b2-u02: If I had known how stressful the job would be, I wouldn't have accepted it so quickly. The salary was attractive, but the hours were long and the meetings endless. If I were you, I'd ask about the workload before signing anything. For many people, flexible working is no longer a luxury but a priority.
dictogloss.en-b2-u03: The minister is said to have known about the problem for months, although she denies it. Many readers no longer trust headlines, and it is easy to see why. Before sharing a story, it is worth checking who wrote it and whether other sources confirm it. A single click can spread misinformation.
dictogloss.en-b2-u04: The experiment must have failed because the samples were not stored at the right temperature. According to the data, energy use has risen by twelve per cent in five years. If nothing changes, prices are bound to increase. Scientists believe that new batteries could solve part of the problem.
dictogloss.en-b2-u05: I wish I had taken my health more seriously when I was younger. For years I couldn't stop worrying about work, and I rarely made time for exercise. Now I try to walk every morning and I've stopped checking emails after eight. It has made a remarkable difference to my mood.
dictogloss.en-b2-u06: Never have I seen a city as colourful as Marrakech. At first, the noise and the crowds were overwhelming, and I experienced a mild culture shock. However, the more I talked to local people, the more I understood the rhythm of daily life. Whether you enjoy a place often depends on your attitude.
dictogloss.en-b2-u07: The company denied having increased its prices without warning, but customers were paying twice as much as the year before. When sales fell, the managers had to cut costs and lay off staff. Economists believe that inflation will slow down, although nobody can predict exactly when.
dictogloss.en-b2-u08: It was my history teacher who taught me to question everything. Schools should prepare students for life, so they need to develop critical thinking as well as knowledge. As a result, many teachers now encourage debates in class. Some argue, however, that exams still matter far more than discussions.
dictogloss.en-b2-u09: Over the past decade, thousands of trees have been planted along the river, and the water has been cleaned. Provided that local businesses continue to cooperate, the area will soon attract wildlife again. Otherwise, the progress could easily be lost. The council has proposed new rules to protect it.
dictogloss.en-b2-u10: Having finished the novel in a single night, I went straight to the bookshop to buy the sequel. The story, in which a young painter discovers a family secret, is beautifully written. What impressed me most was the ending, which was both surprising and moving. I would recommend it to anyone.
dictogloss.en-b2-u11: You needn't have paid the fine, because the parking sign was not clearly visible. Drivers are required to display their tickets, but the council could have made the rules clearer. Many residents have written to the local newspaper, arguing that the system is unfair and needs to be reviewed.
dictogloss.en-b2-u12: Breaking the ice with strangers is not easy for everyone. When I give feedback to colleagues, I try to be tactful: I might say that a report could perhaps be shorter, rather than that it is too long. Making an effort to listen carefully often matters more than finding the perfect words.
dictogloss.en-b2-u13: It's about time I tried something adventurous. What I really want to do is cross the Andes on foot. My friends think it's too risky, but I've been training for months. Last year a sudden storm forced us to turn back, and we spent the night in a tiny hut. I've never felt so alive.
dictogloss.en-b2-u14: Climate change, inequality and migration are closely connected, so no country can deal with them alone. In other words, global problems require global solutions. Although progress has been slow, international agreements have achieved real results. The question is whether governments will act quickly enough to protect future generations.
